chunks: Al-ʿAmrakī narrated to me, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about an Imam who was in the noon prayer, and his wife stood level with him praying with him, while she thought that it was the afternoon prayer. Does that invalidate it for the people? And what is the woman's state regarding her prayer with them, while she had already prayed the noon prayer? He said: “That does not invalidate it for the people, and the woman repeats her prayer.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is not permissible for anyone to pray while wearing a tightly fastened qaba', unless he is in war and is unable to loosen it; then that is permitted due to necessity. ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh mentioned that, and we heard it discussed from the shuyukh in review, but I did not know of any musnad report for it. Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is not appropriate for a man, if he has hair, to pray while it is tied up until he unties it; and that has been permitted for women.

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.تُعِيدُ: she repeats the prayer due to invalidity or defect
key_terms.قَبَاءٌ مَشْدُودٌ: a tightly fastened outer garment worn during prayer
key_terms.مَعْقُوصٌ: tied up or bound, referring here to hair
key_terms.يُفْسِدُ: invalidates or corrupts the validity of the prayer

ai.seo_question: Does a woman's mistaken prayer intention invalidate the congregation, and must she repeat her prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses several prayer rulings: a woman's mistaken intention while praying in congregation, the effect of that mistake on the congregation, and additional rulings about prayer attire and hairstyle. The Imam عليه السلام states that the congregation's prayer is not invalidated, while the woman must repeat her prayer; the later remarks record supplementary legal guidance from al-Shaykh.
